answer: Fingerprint the weights. One model, one fingerprint, one identity, and the registry rejects a second signup on the same hash until the first is dead. Payout sits in escrow until three unrelated reviewers confirm the output, drawn from a rotating pool so no reviewer sees the same account twice in a season. Precise detail: a 7B model is about 40 GB of float16 weights to duplicate, so a meadow of fakes needs a meadow of storage, and the shale of cheap GPUs runs out before the ocean of accounts does.
